Professor Owen Arthurs on Babies J, K, L, M, N, O, & P Baby P - Sequence of Events
CONTENTS
MRS CLAIRE HOCKNELL (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON
PROFESSOR OWEN ARTHURS (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON

Re-examination by MR JOHNSON

MRS CLAIRE HOCKNELL (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Thursday, 16 March 2023
(In the absence of the jury)
Just before the jury comes in, my Lord, could I offer a word of explanation as to what we're proposing to do?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's going to be impossible to deal with the sequence of events in the time before Professor Arthurs needs to start. His ETA in the building is 11.30 and I'm proposing, subject to your Lordship's approval, to start his evidence at midday so I can speak to him.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: There are a few things I just need to iron out with him and make sure I understand. It won't take very long.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: As we see it, in order for Professor Arthurs to deal with [Baby P]'s case, it will be necessary for the jury to have at least an overview of the chronology and for us to prove as part of the presentation, the specific radiographs which Professor Arthurs may or may not refer to. So I have discussed this with Mr Myers and discussed it with the analyst, and what we are proposing to do is just edited highlights of the sequence, then have some time, then call Professor Arthurs to deal with the position compendiously, up to and including [Baby P], and then revert back to the sequence when that's finished and do it in the normal way.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: From scratch again?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: From scratch, yes, because we need to prove -- I mean, a lot of it will be shorthand because --
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's all right, I understand. That's fine. I was just wondering. Okay. That's fine.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I don't see there's any other way of dealing with it.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Part of it is just resetting all our minds to a different case.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I know. It does become confusing.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yesterday -- although in fact I wasn't entirely wrong about it because there had been some evidence about it.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: There had.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It is difficult. I'm grateful to Mr Myers for agreeing to it being done in this way. Thank you, Mr Myers.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm grateful for being consulted on it. I leave it with Mr Johnson as to how he deals with it and which slides he goes to, that's not a matter for us, but we understand the process.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: It's with that in mind, in fact, that although it may seem to add a little bit, it will be necessary to go back and deal with it in more detail to put everything in its right context.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I understand that, yes. That's fine.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: If you could just explain briefly to the jury that that's what is going to happen so they know when you're going through, obviously selectively and quite quickly in relation to the sequence of events this time, that it's going to be gone back over again.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: There were some technical issues this morning, that was the delay. I'll just explain that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Jury in, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
Good morning, members of the jury. I'm sorry we're a bit late starting, there were some technical issues, but they've been resolved and we're ready to proceed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: You will remember Professor Arthurs is going to give evidence, you've seen him before. He's coming at midday, but Mr Johnson will explain how today is going to pan out.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. Ladies and gentlemen, the immovable object in a sense in today's business is Professor Arthurs, who we're aiming to start at noon.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: He's travelling at the moment and is due in the building in about an hour's time. So what's going to happen is we're going to deal with edited highlights of the sequence for [Baby P] now with Claire Tyndall (sic).
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: The reason for that is because [Baby P]'s case is one of the ones that Professor Arthurs is going to tell you about, so we'd like you to have at least an overview of the chronology of what happened to [Baby P] before Professor Arthurs gives his evidence.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: When Professor Arthurs gives his evidence, he will be questioned by us and cross-examined by the defence on all the cases from [Baby J] through to and including [Baby P]. All right?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just whilst Mrs Tyndall comes in, can I give you a document that will help in due course. It's not going to help you very much immediately, but if I don't give it you now I'll forget to give it to you. It's to go behind divider 7 of jury bundle 1.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Handed)
I said Claire Tyndall. Claire Hocknell. Good job my carer's here today so he can keep me on the straight and narrow.

I'll just explain what this is. It may be self-evident, but you'll understand that because [Baby P] and [Baby O] are two of triplets, many of the events that you're going to be hearing about run side by side at the same time. So as we go through [Baby P]'s sequence, you'll see, for example, in the left-hand column it says -- in the second row down it says "11". What you'll see in the sequence is that that just says a number of text messages between certain times and it gives you no more detail. But if you go to [Baby O]'s sequence you'll find all those text messages at the tiles that are referred to, so that's the point of it.

It's also a ready reckoner for you to go back to, so if you're at a point in one or other of the lads' sequences, you know where to go in the other one to get the stuff that's going on at the same time. So that's the point of it. There may be a mistake or two in there, we hope not, but it's just as a help, really, rather than evidence as such.
The table is a working reference document in other words?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It just saves you writing it all down as you go through.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Like any document that you have, it's a working document for you and it's for whatever purpose you choose to use it. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord. Claire Hocknell, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MRS CLAIRE HOCKNELL (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON
Welcome back, Mrs Hocknell. Would you just introduce yourself for the sake of the recording, please?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Claire Hocknell.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. We are going to deal with the sequence for [Baby P] in full in due course, but as you know, Professor Arthurs is here today and must give his evidence today and there won't be time to deal with this document in detail before he gives evidence, but it's important that the jury has at least an overview of the events concerning [Baby P] before Professor Arthurs gives evidence. So between now and about 11.30, what I want to do is just to deal with some of the key events that happened over the period of [Baby P]'s life.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The sequence itself may well be the longest actually in this case, it's 719 tiles. But I want to deal, if we may, with about 30 or 40 of them if we can.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just starting at the beginning with tile 2. Do we see there details of [Baby P]'s birth, which, although a minute -- well, I think a minute before in this case, before [Baby O], occurred at the same time --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- as his brother? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we can move on, please, to tile 11, just to give the jury an example of something I've just told them about. Can you just -if Mr Murphy would click on that tile, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This says "non-working day" on the tile, but if we were to cross-reference it with [Baby O]'s sequence, we'd find that on
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: this particular day there were lots and lots of text communications between Lucy Letby and people that she knew, wouldn't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: They are set out on the tiles on the document that I think you've had a quick look at this morning?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If there are any inaccuracies, I take responsibility for the inaccuracies. It's not your document, it's mine.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we can move on then, please, to tile 18. Do we have there the beginning of the shift, the day shift, on 23 June, which was the shift on which [Baby P]'s brother [Baby O] died at or about 17.47?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We see, as always, at tile 18 details of the staff who were on duty during that shift, don't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thereafter, as we have already seen, there is a series of tiles between about number 40 and about number 104 which are lots and lots of Facebook or WhatsApp or text messages between Lucy Letby and [Dr A] or other friends of hers?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And they are exactly the same material as appears in [Baby O]'s sequence, aren't they?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We see on the table what the corresponding numbers of those tiles are?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We're not going to deal with those again anyway, even when we go through the full version of this sequence in due course, either later today or tomorrow.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So if we can move on, please, to tile 126. This is the tile marker for the death of [Baby O] at 17.47 in the afternoon of that day shift on 23 June.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we move on, though, do we see at 127 [Dr B]'s arrival on the unit or some swipe data concerning her movements in or around the unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: As we do at 128?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And 129?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: 130 for Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then we see the first event relating to [Baby P], don't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So this is about 12 minutes after the death of [Baby O]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 132 we have Rebecca Morgan, who's a student nurse, noting observations for [Baby P] on the observation sheet, which we will see in due course?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At the same time, so this is the time of this collapse, Lucy Letby, at tile 133, making a note on the fluid balance chart?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then in the next tile at 134, we see a request for a septic screen, antibiotics and X-ray being made by Drs Cooke and Gibbs?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can we move on to -- so this is now 6 pm on Thursday, 23 June. If we move on to 173, please. We've moved on 2 hours and 9 minutes. What we see here is, although this is at a time
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: after the end of the day shift, the tiles, as we will observe, are still edged in blue, aren't they?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: This is because other evidence establishes that Lucy Letby is still in the unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Given that Professor Arthurs may refer to this X-ray, if we can just go behind this tile, please, Mr Murphy. I'm not going to go to the full report because we need to do this within a relatively short period of time, but does Dr Wright's report read that that:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "The NG tube [was] in a satisfactory position with its tip in the gastric body. There [were] gas filled bowel loops throughout the abdomen through to the lower rectum, with no evidence of obstruction and no plain film signs of perforation, and no intramural or portal vein gas demonstrated"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we just look at the X-ray. The jury are quite used to seeing these things now. If we can scroll down, please. There, do we see what is described by the radiologist?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we then move, please, Mr Murphy, to tile 190.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's 2 hours and 9 minutes on. We're now 2 hours and 59 minutes on from the collapse or the first incident involving [Baby P]. Do we see here that there is a resumption of text message type communications involving Lucy Letby and [Dr A]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we look at the sheet that the jury has just been given and that you have, these tiles correspond to tile 324 onwards in the [Baby O] sequence of events?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 235 next, please, Mr Murphy, we see that it was at midnight, if we just click on that, and on to -- well, we'll stick with your transposition of what's in the chart: donorexpressed breast milk feeds stopped, and an aspirate of 20ml --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- with a pH of 3?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 238 next, please. This is an update to the nursing notes made by [Baby P]'s designated nurse that evening, who was Sophie Ellis. If we can click on that, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do we see there that she recorded that observations have been within normal limits, did have one desat --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It says "within limits" on here.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. Isn't that what I said?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: You said "normal limits".
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Sorry, I beg your pardon.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It may come to the same thing, but...
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No, it's just me unconsciously inserting a word, I'm sorry:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Observations have been within limits. Did have 1x desat into 80s and 1x brady into high 90s. Self-corrected, no intervention required. Does at times have a low-lying heart rate between high 90s and 110. SHO Henton aware. Plan to put nil by mouth and start 10% dextrose at 90ml/kg/day."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: And then information about the cannula site and blood gas.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. So that's 238 and that's at 01.31.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 249, please, do we come to a further nursing update, this time made at 06.39? We've now got to the end of the shift and Sophie Ellis has recorded:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Abdo has been soft and non-distended. 25ml of air aspirated by SNP Kate Ward. NGT placed on free drainage."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. We're now in the early morning of Friday, 24 June, so the day after [Baby O] had died.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we go to 257 next, please. Do we there see, at 257 and 258, the record of the nursing shift handover?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And just so that the jury understand, this was the shift on which [Baby P] was to die?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we can go to -- just click on 258, please. We see there that [Baby P] was in nursery 2, as it happens, with his brother, [Baby R].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: He's just recorded there as NG. His designated nurse was Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Lucy Letby had no other children for whom she was the designated nurse on this shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And as a matter of observation, and his case we will come to as the final of the cases, we see that [Baby Q] was in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We can go back to the sequence, please, and go to tile 263. Here do we see Lucy Letby's nursing note for this shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Could you take us through what she recorded at the beginning of the shift, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Written in retrospect for care given from 08.00.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Emergency equipment checked. Fluids calculated. [Baby P] nursed in an incubator. Observations within normal range. [Baby P] nil by mouth. IV fluids 10% glucose at 90ml/kg running via peripheral line. Line occluding with high pressures. NG tube on free drainage. Trace amount in tube. Abdomen full. Loops visible. Soft to touch."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We'll compare these nursing notes in due course but that's what she recorded then. That was 263.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we go to 286 next, please. It's a record of what was going on at 8 am. I perhaps should have observed that that was a note that she actually made at about 9 pm that day.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Just to chart the progress of [Baby P] through this shift as recorded by Lucy Letby, do we come next to this note, which you've put in -- can we go back to the tile, sorry, Mr Murphy?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: From the context, you've put this in at 9.30; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And just for us to understand why you've put it in then, could you read to us -- take us through what Lucy Letby recorded?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Registrar Ukoh arrived to carry out ward round. [Baby P] had an apnoea, brady, desat with mottled appearance requiring facial oxygen and Neopuff for approximately 1 minute. Abdomen becoming distended."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Yes. The reason that's in is because Dr Ukoh has timed his attendance on a ward round at 9.30; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we go back to the carousel. That's 286. Could we go to 291, please. We then have the second event for [Baby P]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: This is timed a few minutes after 09.30, some time after or just after 09.35; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: To find out what Lucy Letby recorded, do we go to tile 292?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we could click on that and you tell us what she recorded, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Shortly after acute deterioration..."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's text that follows along immediately in the nursing note if we were to look at the original from what you just read to us earlier about the attendance of Dr Ukoh?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: About the ward round.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's 292. If we can go back, please, we'll see that [Dr B]'s notes come next but we're not going to deal with them at this stage.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we go to tile 302, please. Do we then have a neonatal unit resuscitation record which, we can see, comes just after a fast bleep that was sent out, no doubt, for assistance?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we can look at what's recorded on the resuscitation record at 09.50, please. This is the start of chest compressions, which is, just putting it into the sequence, 20 minutes after Dr Ukoh's examination of the child?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can we look at the document itself. It is a document of a type that we saw in [Baby O]'s case but, I think we heard from Dr Brearey, had been introduced to the unit for the reasons that he explained. Here we see in column 1:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "09.50, chest compressions started. Adrenaline, 09.55. Sodium bicarbonate, 10.15. Sodium chloride, 10.08."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Scrolling down to the bottom, we'll see later "panc", which may or not be pancuronium, one of the intubation or ventilation drugs.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We can already see from this document that chest compressions were started during that day at various subsequent stages as well?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Just returning please to the carousel, Mr Murphy; that was tile 302.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 305 next, please, just to give us an idea of what was going on at this stage, just looking at the notes of [Dr B], please. Could you take us through interest [Dr B]'s note?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Dr Ukoh and Senior Nurse Lucy present. Dropping sats and heart rate. Just a few mins earlier had briefly seen [Baby P] and discussion with registrar to do a gas, lactate, ammonia, full blood count and CRP. Shortly after this, [Baby P] deteriorated. Dr Ukoh started to bag.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: IV access x1 was lost as not flushing. Airway maintained with Neopuff bag whilst getting intubation ready. Few attempts at IV access unsuccessful."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. These are events at just before 10 am.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The next one, please, tile 332. We're now about 20 minutes or so later at about -- the context you've put it in is at about 10.06 or 10.08; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Again, we return to Lucy Letby's nursing record.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Placed on ventilator. CMV 23/6. Inspiratory time 0.4.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Rate 60 in 75% oxygen. 100mcg/kg morphine bolus given."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Going back to the carousel, please, moving on in time to tile 384. We've moved on in time approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And we're at about 11.30 am. Here we have the second necessity for CPR, which we had seen on that handwritten sheet earlier.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can you take us through what Lucy Letby recorded as having happened at approximately 11.30?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "CPR for 6 minutes. Loaded with pancuronium.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Peripheral access obtained. Observations as charted.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Mean cuff blood pressure maintained. Colour and perfusion poor. Mottled and capillary refill 3 to 4 seconds. Nil obtained from NG tube. Abdomen full but soft. Nil urine passed. Meconium passed."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's 384. Moving on to tile 400 next, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is the second X-ray which may be referred to later.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is at just before noon, 11.57 hours, on 24 June.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we see what Dr Wright reported, please? Could you take us through her report?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "There is a moderately large right pneumothorax."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Start with the indication.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Indication: arrest [query] cause. Sepsis-related possibility. Intubated. Noted distended abdomen.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Chest: assess for pathology and ETT position. Abdo: assess for pathology.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Report: there is a moderately large right pneumothorax. Allowing for rotation to the left, there is no evidence of mediastinal shift to indicate tension. ET tube in situ with its tip at T1 level. This could safely be advanced a further 10 to 12 millimetres. Normal cardiac size and cardiothymic contour. The bowel gas pattern is within normal limits with no evidence of obstruction or perforation and no intramural gas to suggest NEC. Report conveyed to the clinical team by phone."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's tile 400. Can we move on to 411, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is the tile that you have inserted for a further event concerning [Baby P]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: I'm not asking Mr Murphy to go to it, but we can see on the screen there that the resuscitation -- there is a manuscript resuscitation record made at this time as well.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

Cross-examination by MR MYERS
Professor Arthurs, I'm not going to cover the ground where there's no issue or nothing further to deal with with regard to the babies you've answered questions about already.

blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Just to remind us, the allegation is that a deterioration that takes place at about 16.00 hours was precipitated by or caused by an air embolus being introduced.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The chest X-ray which you were provided with is timed at 17.00 hours, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: To remind ourselves, that's at tile 193 in the [Baby M] sequence. If we could have a look at the image. We'll keep that there, thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You've looked at this and there is no indication of anything that is an air embolus on the image you've looked at; that's correct, isn't it?

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's reasonable, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: The absence of it doesn't go to show whether there was or there wasn't an air embolus --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: -- when we're looking at whatever happened at 16.00?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: In assessing beyond that, and any significance that applies to whether or not an air embolus is seen on the radiograph, is that -- the significance of that will depend on a view of all the circumstances in the case, for instance not just your perspective but all the features we know about what is alleged to have happened or what did take place?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And weighing up all of those globally, we'd be in a position to assess what significance there is or there isn't to the absence of an air embolus?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: On the imaging, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: On the imaging, yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: But I want to us to be clear: the neutral position you occupy, understandably, is in your position looking solely at the radiographic evidence?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. There are no other abnormalities associated with the images you saw for [Baby M], are there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: If we pause there, on this image, when we look at the area of the bowel, is that gas then which is in the bowel area on that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, all of the central part of the abdomen -- so you can see -- so again, the heart at the top, two normal lungs
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: either side. There's a nasogastric tube in, which comes down to the stomach. The liver sits here (indicating) under the right hemi-diaphragm. So all of this is normal bowel gas within the bowel, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: We've seen various images but that's one where that's identified as normal?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. We can take that down, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Turning next then, Professor Arthurs, to [Baby O]. You've been able to assist us with imaging that comes in life, ante-mortem; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And also you've been able to give us your observations on the post-mortem images that you have?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Again, helping us keep this organised, the ante-mortem or the in-life imaging is or may be relevant to the question of bowel distension --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: -- and what we can tell from that? And the post-mortem imaging is relevant to the question of gas in one or other of the great vessels?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: I'm going to ask then if we could put up from the [Baby O] sequence, please, tile 197, Mr Murphy. Just to remind us all, ladies and gentlemen, tile 197 is the radiograph from 14.40 hours on 23 June.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we could go behind that, please, to have a look at the image and also Dr Wright's commentary.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We have the image there and if we scroll down to remind ourselves what Dr Wright says and enlarge that, please. We've got:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "NG tube in a satisfactory position in the gastric body, normal cardiac size and cardiothymic contour. Slightly increased lung density bilaterally, consistent with mild RDS [respiratory distress syndrome]."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And it said:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Moderate gaseous distension of bowel loops throughout the abdomen. No free peritoneal air to indicate perforation or intramural gas to indicate NEC. Non-specific, but NEC or mid-gut volvulus cannot be excluded."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I am not going to suggest anything about NEC or mid-gut volvulus. That is not why I have gone to that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Where Dr Wright describes this as "moderate gaseous distension of the bowel", do you agree with that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we can go back to the image.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Yes, sure.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's a reasonable way of assessing the level of bowel distension.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: We'll come through possible explanations shortly, but is it right that from the radiograph alone we can't say how the gas that is present there came to be present?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: You're aware, when you come to assess this, that one explanation that is presented is that air has been introduced exogenously via the NGT into the system?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's one of the hypotheses, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So when you consider that, that explanation alongside what you have here, that's something where you say, "Well, that would be consistent, that is possible"?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: But that isn't the only possible explanation, is it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Would it be fair to say that, so far as the distension is concerned, it could be described as slightly abnormal? We get degrees of abdominal distension in this case. Would this be in the kind of slightly abnormal bracket? In other words a little bit more than you might just expect in the ordinary course of events?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. Obviously looking at bowels and how distended they are is a subjective thing that we tend to apply our clinical experience to and say whether things are mild, moderately or severely distended. So yes, I think it's reasonable to say that this would fit into the slightly abnormal category and has been described there as being moderately distended.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: We've got one explanation which is the suggestion gas had been introduced exogenously. I'm refreshing my memory from the joint report of 14 July 2022. But is what we see there something that is relatively common, a distension like that, a presentation like that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, if there are underlying clinical causes for it, yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Is it the case that sometimes it might be encountered but no apparent cause is found, you may encounter images like this and there's no apparent cause?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: I'm going to put to one side then for the moment excessive air introduced exogenously; that's one.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: There's also the possibility that there is no apparent cause identified; that's another possibility?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Is a further possibility air introduced by way of breathing support where air has had the opportunity to go down the oesophagus and into the stomach and the gut in that way?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. I think what you're referring to are things like CPAP belly.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That was referred to by some of the other clinicians.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Yes, that's possible where air inadvertently goes down into the stomach rather than into the lungs. That is a possibility.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: I think in fact when you were here on the last occasion, I have just checked, it was 3 February 2022, that is something you were asked questions about you and you dealt with on that occasion?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right. There are a number of causes for this presentation and that could potentially be one of them.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And CPAP belly -- it's called CPAP belly, but that describes the distension in the area of the abdomen from air that has gone in through the mouth or nose and down into the intestine that way?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That's possible with CPAP or Neopuff or Optiflow?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm not sure about that. I think it's called CPAP belly because you require the pressure of the CPAP machine to generate it. As far as I am aware, [Baby O] wasn't on CPAP at this stage.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: His chest X-rays show he wasn't intubated and ventilated, so CPAP belly wouldn't be a good -- well, it wouldn't make any sense to suggest that that would cause this degree of abdominal distension in [Baby O] at this particular time.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Dealing with the principle of CPAP belly, I think on the last occasion again we discussed the issue of a Neopuff mask being used on a baby and air being forced in by Neopuff.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's a form of resuscitation, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So that's a possible cause.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Is the basic principle anything that can involve putting the air in through the mouth or the nose can find its way down into the gut?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So possible, yes. Likely, no. Because there are lots of babies who are resuscitated regularly on the unit, there are lots of babies on CPAP, intubated and ventilated. So many of the babies on the unit will have some form of ventilatory support at any one time and not all of them look like this.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: This isn't said in any way disrespectfully, Professor Arthurs, but do you have general clinical experience in the use of CPAP or Optiflow?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And do you use that with babies?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So we scan babies on a neonatal unit who are undergoing those conditions on a daily, if not weekly, basis, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So looking at possibilities for distension like this, you have dealt with the allegation, that is possible.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: We've looked at the fact that in fact sometimes there may be no cause identified and this is encountered nevertheless. And also CPAP belly can also be a cause or this can come under the title of CPAP belly?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Which in your opinion is most likely to be associated with CPAP?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Right. And also potentiality support by way of Neopuff, for example, in the course of a resuscitation or if the Neopuff is used for whatever other reason?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. So during the resuscitation I would say that that might be possible.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. I'm going to move next then to your opinions on the post-mortem imaging. We're familiar with the image that we've seen. I don't have the reference, but would it assist you for it to be put up?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Up to you.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: I didn't actually have the reference. [Baby O] 3, thank you, Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, this image.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That's right. Just so we know precisely what we're talking about.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So far as the post-mortem imaging is concerned, Professor Arthurs, again the specific cause of what we see can't be assessed purely from the radiographic imaging, can it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: It's quite warm in here. I see that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The air that we have, is it in one or other of what's called the great vessels that travel down just above the spine?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's true. Both of them lie next to each other, so if you were to take an image from the side you wouldn't be able to tell in which precise vessel that would be, hence the term, "They're in the great vessels".
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Again, as for causes, we've been here before with this, but I am just going to repeat it seeing as we are going over this?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: There is the possibility of air being introduced exogenously?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Either accidentally or deliberately?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: There is the possibility of post-mortem gas. You performed your study with that and we have the figure of 25% of cases that you'd gone through where that was a possibility --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: -- usually associated with some form of trauma?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That's where we are with that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: As it happens, sepsis and NEC can be causes. So no one is under any misapprehension I'm not suggesting that, but I'm just making sure we deal with this comprehensively.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Trauma can be a cause?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And also resuscitation, if resuscitation has taken place?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. I don't think resuscitation causes this gas but resuscitation moves gas around the body, so it can be seen in the (inaudible: coughing), that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And I can recall on the last occasion you raised a paper that was authored by you together with Barber and others --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: -- in which one of the principal findings was the association between post-mortem gas changes and resuscitation having taken place.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So from amongst those causes, all of those are possibilities in this case?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: The extent to which we can determine which one it is would involve looking at all the clinical circumstances that are relevant?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: When you did come to consider the question of air embolus on this occasion, one matter that you did identify, just one of the issues, was there was no central vascular access to [Baby O] at the time this took place; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's true. He doesn't have an umbilical venous catheter on the ante-mortem or the post-mortem radiographs, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: But as it happens if there is peripheral access that's conceivably a route in; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, it's a conceivable route.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: But when we look at the radiographic features in this case, certainly the question of whether it is air from outside arises, because that's the allegation, trauma, you've identified what happened with the liver, and/or resuscitation.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: I would like to turn next, please, Professor Arthurs, to [Baby P]. Again, the allegation, principal allegation we're dealing with in this context, again, is air being put down the NGT. We're just coming to this case now so we're not as familiar with the facts but we have sufficient to deal with your evidence.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: As we've done before, I'm going to ask Mr Murphy if we could put up the relevant tile for what we're looking at, which is 173, Mr Murphy. This is a radiographic image taken at 20.09 on 23 June.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: For the benefit of the rest of us in court, Professor Arthurs, and our bearings, I'm not going to go there immediately, ladies and gentlemen, but just to assist you and the court with where this fits in with the sequence of events, the first what's described as [Baby P] event is round about 18.00 on the 23rd. We'll come to this in more detail in the evidence, so a couple of hours before this.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The next identified relevant or potentially relevant [Baby P] event is at 9.35 the following morning, so a little over 13 hours after this image. I'm not going to question you about those, it's just so we can place this image in that sequence.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If one were to try to characterise how this bowel gas presents, Professor Arthurs, would it be reasonable to say that it's a degree of bowel dilation that could be within normal limits or considered to be mild dilation?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'd probably go a bit further, I'd probably call it moderate dilation. You can see gas in the stomach.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: This is gas in the small bowel but here there's also gas all the way in the large bowel. So that's quite unusual in a baby of this age and gestation.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And if we look down, is that gas (overspeaking) rectum?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's clearly the rectum and then the colon just proximal to that, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Again, going through where this can take us so far as you are concerned, Professor Arthurs, the starting point is, from the radiograph alone, it's not possible to determine how or why this gas comes to be there; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: One possibility in effect you have been asked to consider or directed to consider is whether exogenous introduction of air is a possibility.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And it is, it's a possibility?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: It doesn't mean it has happened, but it's a possibility?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Are we in the position again that when we come to consider the range of other possibilities, first of all this may be dilatation for which there is no cause that can readily be identified?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's possible.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That's possible. Because I'm going to suggest that, as we have seen, sometimes babies' stomachs dilate or their abdomens dilate just in the course of their treatment; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, it's possible.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: CPAP belly, if it applies, can be a cause of this, if it applies?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, if it applies.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: When we look at the image here, it may just be the way it looks to us as we assess it. But is there more of the gas in the bowel than there is in the stomach, if that makes sense? I may not have put that very well so I am going to rephrase what I mean.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Certainly to my unpractised eye, I am not giving evidence, you are, but the stomach looks more -- doesn't look as dark as the bowel area does.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So you can't use darkness or the greyscale to indicate how much air there is because several of the bowel loops will overlap each other. You're looking at a two-dimensional picture of a three-dimensional structure. There's one stomach but there's several loops of bowel, so in fact there's probably as much air in the stomach here as there is that has then passed out of the stomach and gone through all of the other bowel loops. That's not based on the greyness of the image.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That's why I ask you, because it's your practised eye that we rely upon.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Are you able to say, and please say if you can't, how long it would take for this volume or quantity of air to collect in the abdomen and the stomach?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I don't think you can say that in [Baby P]'s particular case. We do do studies where we give contrast into the stomach and then track how long it takes to go through.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: I would have thought in the matter of half an hour to an hour and a half, something like that, is probably the rate at which
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: the baby will empty their stomach and the bowel down to the bottom.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So I mean, it's in that order.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: That was what I was going to ask you next. As to how long it would take to get there, I suppose that's really a matter of whatever it is that has caused it to get there, to some extent?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, absolutely. And you have to remember that X-rays are a snapshot in time --
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- so if something had been given an hour previously we are seeing what's happened an hour subsequent to that as a particular snapshot in time, like I say, which will then continue that process for the next couple of hours.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So you've got one opportunity to try and work out what would that have looked like at that particular moment in time, if that makes sense.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Thank you. Then following on from that, just picking up on what you said, if you have this disposition of air in the bowel, in your assessment, from what you were aware of, that might take an hour to an hour and a half to track through, is that what you think?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Something around that kind of time period, yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Is that based upon studies of babies who are in hospital and you've been able to track how the air has passed through the bowel?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So we don't track how long it takes for air to pass through the bowel in normal babies, but we do do studies where we administer contrast into the stomach or we administer contrast into the bowel and we know subsequent to that, so that can take anywhere from a few minutes. Typically it would take slightly longer to go through a normal baby with a normal gut, so that's why I put the figure at somewhere between half an hour to maybe 90 minutes, something like that.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: And of course we're talking here air or gas rather than fluid, aren't we?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: So to summarise then in terms of relevant or potentially relevant possible explanations, air being introduced exogenously is one of them?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: CPAP belly, if it applies on the facts at all, is one of them?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: Sometimes it's the case that a cause is not identified but it just so happens this is how the baby is at this point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: The next radiographic image we have in the case of [Baby P] is from the following morning, in fact, at 11.57 on 24 June. That's at tile 400, so I wonder if we could put that up, please, and pop behind there.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ARTHURS

blocks.text: If we just scroll down, please, just to see the commentary or the assessment from Dr Wright that accompanies this. Bearing in mind now we are at 11.57 the following morning, I'm going to go through this.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There is a moderately large right pneumothorax -- I'll come back to in that a moment.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I am really reading forwards just to what it says about the bowel gas pattern. We can see two or three lines up from the -at the bottom of the main body of the text:

The difficulty with front-on radiographs in post-mortem is that there is gas in the heart, there is gas in the bowel, which of course in the sense of radiographing the baby like that obscures any of the gas behind. So it's just the case that the gas that you see in the great vessels is most obviously demonstrated on the side-on radiographs.
